findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the corpus-eligibility rule's container screen explicitly (exclude G3/G4/decomp-shape cases lacking a non-empty `children` list) and fix or replace the G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar worked example, which as written errors rather than producing a decision.
evidence: Plan: 'A case is eligible when its expect is in {finding, fail, pass} AND its solver id … resolves to a non-agentic run_case arm.' — no container-children screen
Plan worked example: 'dataset case G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar … carries expect: finding and criterion: G3 … Its three v2 epochs return findings / findings / no-findings'
plan-review-container.eval.yaml:85 — G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar has `criterion: G3`, `expect: finding`, inline `input`, and NO `children` list
eval_solver.py:110-115 — a container criterion (CONTAINER_CRITERIA=('G3','G4','decomp-shape'), pass1.py:46) with no non-empty `children` raises ValueError
provider_parity_results.json:32-42,573-583 — this exact case is recorded as 'ValueError: container criterion G3 needs a non-empty children list …', i.e. it errored, not decided
findings.finding: The plan's stated corpus-eligibility rule does not exclude CONTAINER criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) that lack a `children` payload, and its own worked example (G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar) is such a case — it carries inline `input` and no `children`, so run_case raises a ValueError (eval_solver.py:110-115) instead of producing the findings/findings/no-findings decision the plan narrates.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' (eligibility rule + worked example)
scenarios: Corpus selector as specified admits G3/G4 gold cases that only raise, burning an epoch on both arms and inflating error counts instead of yielding a verdict
An implementer following the worked example would expect a recall hit where the run actually produces an error
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the eligibility rule: 'and, for a CONTAINER criterion (G3/G4/decomp-shape per pass1.CONTAINER_CRITERIA), the case carries a non-empty `children` list — a container case with only inline `input` raises in run_case and is not corpus.' Then either pick a container fixture that supplies `children`, or use a non-container criterion, for the worked example.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a THIRD eligibility clause to the corpus rule excluding polarity-free solvers (scorers with no block/advisory verdict, e.g. `code-review-verify`), co-located with the `_verdict_decision` mapping, and re-derive the eligible-case and sample counts (142 / 30) after that exclusion.
evidence: Plan: "A case is eligible when its `expect` is in `{finding, fail, pass}` AND its solver id … resolves to a non-agentic `run_case` arm." — only the three agentic reviewers are named as exclusions.

`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-verify.eval.yaml`:4,19 — "scored on PRESENCE of verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK verdict" / "scored independently of any FAIL/BLOCK polarity"; dataset carries `expect: finding` (V-real-defect) and `expect: pass` (V-clean-rename); gold_set uses `label: useful`.
`fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` keys only on `verdict`/`findings` (fidelity_spot_eval.py:83-86); a verifications-only output has neither, so it falls through to `advisory`.

The landed implementation carries a SEPARATE `POLARITY_FREE_SOLVERS = {"code-review-verify"}` exclusion (src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:89-101) — a second exclusion class the plan text never mentions — kept distinct from `AGENTIC_SOLVERS` precisely because "collapsing them would lose one".
findings.finding: The corpus-eligibility rule as stated (gold `expect` value AND a non-agentic run_case arm) would select `code-review-verify` cases, but that solver's output is presence-scored with no block/advisory polarity, so `_verdict_decision` maps every case to `advisory` and the gold-`finding` case becomes a guaranteed false miss on both arms — corrupting the criterion-(b) flip count and criterion-(c) recall. The plan's mapping/enum is not co-located with a polarity-free exclusion that the scoring requires.
findings.location: Plan §"Corpus and the gold floor" (eligibility rule + "142 eligible cases across 15 specs" / "30 items"); worked-example paragraph
scenarios: An executor selects the corpus by the plan's stated rule, includes code-review-verify's finding/pass cases, and both arms miss the gold-block case — either inflating decision_flips or silently depressing recall below the 2pp margin.
The recorded 30-item / 142-eligible corpus math in the plan is off because it counts polarity-free cases the mapping cannot score.
findings.suggested_fix: State the eligibility predicate as three parts — gold `expect`, non-agentic arm, AND a solver whose output carries block/advisory polarity readable by `_verdict_decision` — and name `code-review-verify` (and any other presence-only scorer) as an excluded solver in a `POLARITY_FREE_SOLVERS`-style constant distinct from the agentic set, with the rationale that a presence scorer would map every case to `advisory` and manufacture false misses.

findings.finding: The plan reuses `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` as THE decision rule for all pooled arms and calls it 'the same two-bucket mapping', but that rule reads only the `verdict`/`findings` keys and does not handle the `code-review-verify` arm's `{verifications:[...]}` output vocabulary — which the plan's own eligibility rule admits — so every verify case is scored `advisory`, forcing a guaranteed recall miss on its gold-block case.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' ("the same two-bucket mapping fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision already uses") and Scope → provider_parity.py 'the epoch-majority ItemRecord adapter'
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend the adapter to treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block` (mirroring the presence contract code-review-verify.eval.yaml scores on), or add code-review-verify to the excluded-spec set alongside the three agentic ops; whichever is chosen, state it in the adapter's worked example so the verify output shape is handled explicitly.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

verify command `grep -rnE '\bprovider_parity\b' .github/workflows/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
